title: Stop idle circling: a dragon going round the same few tiles without eating must go and explore
hypothesis: Our online games (submission 3976, 106 games) show 78 runs of 30+ rounds where one of our dragons went round at most 4 tiles eating nothing; the longest were 225 rounds (game 122872) and 220 (121980). In game 126659 (data/replays/126659.replay in the main checkout, our side B) dragon 13, length 2, circled a 2x2 at 26-27,8-9 from round 72 to 123 with nothing in view, while pearls spawned 4 tiles away at 22,5 22,7 22,8 and 24,4. We are also hungry more often than opponents (46.5 vs 36.7 stretches of 40+ rounds per game without eating while pearls were in view). First find the cause in the champion code: follow such a dragon with `.venv/bin/python /Users/me/Dev/unsw-battlecode-2026/tools/watch.py dragon REPLAY --id N --rounds A-B` and `frames ... --around N` on /Users/me/Dev/unsw-battlecode-2026/data/replays/{122872,121980,125780,121707,126659}.replay (our side: 122872 B, 121980 A, 125780 A, 121707 A, 126659 B; `scan FILE --team SIDE` finds the circling runs). Likely suspects: no explore target when the known map looks fresh, a target equal to the current tile, or a safety/dead-end rule that closes every exit. Fix the cause so a dragon with nothing worth doing nearby explores (including revisiting stale areas and known pearl tiles). Scenarios: a lone short dragon with no pearl in view and pearls just outside it leaves the loop; a dragon waiting beside a pearl tile about to spawn still waits; count idle circling in quick-check games before and after.

title: Keep last turn's pearl target unless a new one is clearly cheaper
hypothesis: Measure the switch rate first. Evidence: a logging copy of champion c0e9ff0 (moves unchanged; self-play on big_empty, unswbc 1.0.0) changed its pearl target without having eaten on 33-38% of dragon-turns in every 100-round bucket. On 12.3% of all turns (2,741 of 22,283), the step taken moved away from the target it picked the very next turn. Half of spawn-tile runs last one turn (2,231 of 4,914), and each distinct spawn target is picked up about 5 separate times. Example, dragon 0, r29-37: targets spawn (13,12) -> shared (22,0) -> remembered (12,7) -> spawn (13,12) -> shared (22,0) -> spawn (11,9), moves N,N,N,W,S,S,S,E. Why the old target was dropped (4,509 switches, r<300): about 40% a teammate or enemy now gets there first (Targets::someoneElseFirst; 28% on spawn tiles, where 63% of the yields were to a strictly nearer teammate, 13% an equal-distance tie the lower id wins, and 3.6% we were nearer but tied on eat time because both equal ready), about 37% the target stopped being a candidate, about 22% pruned because a candidate with a lower rough cost was found, 0.4% evaluated and beaten on cost. Online, on Big Empty (r10-40), teams 206, 609 and 450, which beat us there, cover 6.3-9.1 tiles per 10 rounds against our 4.2-6.3, see a pearl on 38-51% of turns against our 25-28%, and have split children 15-20 tiles from their parent 20 rounds later against our 10-13. Change, behind its own switch, in Targets::choosePearl (bot/targets.hpp): remember last turn's target tile and cost. If that tile is still a candidate that passes every existing check (reach, spawnSlack, someoneElseFirst), evaluate it even when rough-cost pruning would skip it, and keep it unless the best alternative's cost is lower by at least P.retargetMargin (start 2 steps). For a future spawn, break an equal-eat-time tie with a teammate by path distance before id. someoneElseFirst against a strictly nearer head still drops the target. Scenarios: (1) held target A at cost 6, new candidate B at cost 5: keep A. (2) B at cost 3: switch. (3) Boundary: B exactly P.retargetMargin cheaper: switch. (4) A eaten or gone: switch. (5) A strictly nearer teammate appears: switch as today. (6) First turn with no previous target: identical to the champion. Report the switch-without-eating rate, steps away from the next target, pearls per 100 dragon-turns in r0-300, and alive/total at r100 and r300 on big_empty, schooltime and default, before and after. Expect a small effect: the switches it can remove (pruned ones plus spawn ties) are about a quarter of all switches.

title: Young split children pick explore targets away from where they were born
hypothesis: Our swarm stays clumped on open maps. Online, 4521 on Big Empty, r10-40, against the teams that beat us there (206, 609, 450) and 524: teammate heads in our 7x7 view 0.85-0.92 per dragon-turn against their 0.43-0.66; a pearl in view on 25-28% of turns against 38-51%. Parent and child are 10.4-12.6 tiles apart 20 rounds after a split, against 14.8-19.9. Their eating rate in r30-60 is 0.10-0.11 per dragon-turn against our 0.07-0.09, and by r60 they have 138-184 total length against our 83-107. Our self-play gives the same 11-12.6 separation, so it is our bot's trait. In a logging copy (self-play, big_empty/schooltime/default), a child's first 10 turns are 33-40% explore targets, median 7-11 path steps away. 84% of its targets are on its own side of the parent, so it is not chasing the parent's pearls: it just stays local. Caveat: in 2 of our 3 Big Empty losses we had caught up by r300 and lost after it (merge-cascade collapse), so the payoff is uncertain; this changes only explore-target choice, not pearl or spawn targeting, so it does not take eating time away (unlike E0036/E0043). Change, behind its own switch, in Targets::bestStaleTile (bot/targets.hpp): for a dragon within P.childLeaveRounds (start 15) of its first turn, add P.childLeaveWeight (start 2) x min(torusDist(t, birthTile), P.exploreFriendCap) to each candidate's score, where birthTile is its head on its first turn. Starting dragons and older dragons are unchanged. Scenarios: (1) a child 3 rounds old, 3 steps east of its birth tile, with equally stale grid tiles 6 steps east and 6 steps west: it picks east. (2) Boundary: the same dragon at age P.childLeaveRounds + 1 scores as today. (3) A child with a visible pearl target keeps the pearl. (4) Starting dragons are unaffected. Report parent-child distance 10 and 20 rounds after a split, teammate heads in view, pearl-in-view share and pearls per dragon-turn in r10-100, and total at r60/r100/r300 on big_empty and two open generated maps.

title: A dense pearl field in view counts like a farm: extend its target reach by the pearls around it
hypothesis: Change, behind a new switch P.clusterYield with P.clusterPearlWeight (start 0.5): in targets.hpp yieldAt, a tile's yield also counts pearls we see or remember now (w.pearlNow, or a pearl seen within P.pearlMemoryRounds) within P.farmClusterRadius, P.clusterPearlWeight each, capped by a new P.clusterYieldCap (start 4). Candidates with yield > 1 already use the real path (headField) and reach P.maxTargetDist * yield, so a 10-pearl field 40 steps away becomes worth the walk, while a lone pearl stays at 14. someoneElseFirst still spreads teammates. Why: on walled maps our dragons spend many turns looking at a pearl field they won't walk to. Share of dragon-turns (r0-400) with 3 or more pearls in view, none within 14 steps by the real kelp map, us vs them: Schooltime 7.7% vs 1.9% (242182) and 7.4% vs 2.1% (241928), Stronghold 8.4% vs 3.8% (241931). It is 0% on Big Empty. In 242182 at r100, four of our dragons at (6-19, 0-2) had 10-15 pearls of the y 37-39 band in view one kelp edge away. The real path is ~45 steps, which we never walked, while 370 ate 253 pearls in our half of that band. yieldAt counts only fast tiles we have watched reset, so a dense field we haven't farmed has yield 1. This is the map-agnostic half of the map-book idea: it needs no portal knowledge, only a walkable path. Scenarios: (1) 12 visible pearls within radius 2 of a tile whose real path is 35 steps, nothing closer: the dragon targets it. (2) Boundary: 2 pearls 20 steps away: ignored as today. (3) A pearl 5 steps away beats the far field (cost divided by yield, capped). (4) Enemy heads nearer the field: yieldToEnemyCloser still applies. (5) No visible cluster: identical to the champion. Measure: turns seeing unreachable clusters, pearls eaten r0-200 on schooltime, stronghold and far-farm generated maps, and deaths on the way (long trips through contested ground).

title: Blind dragons keep their heading: explore ties go straight ahead, not to the grid's scan order (today a north-then-west bias)
hypothesis: Audit of bot/targets.hpp (review 2026-09-26), measured on replays. Mechanism: Targets::chooseExplore replaces the explore target as soon as it is visible, and bestStaleTile samples a grid of stride P.exploreStride (4) aligned on our head, so on open ground the candidates are the tiles exactly 4 steps ahead, left and right (just outside the 7x7 view), all unseen (staleCap) and tied on 3*stale - 2*dist; the strict '>' keeps the first in scan order (lowest y, then lowest x), so a blind dragon turns north when it can, else west, and one step later the new target is in view and is replaced again. Friend spacing (visible teammates only) and staleness break some ties. Measured on our online replays (tools/watch.py plus small replay scripts): on Big Empty r0-99, in all 7 games of 6518/6542 and on both sides, 33-39% of our blind moves (no pearl in view) go north and 17-23% south (opponents 26-38% north). Blind moves keep the previous heading 43-45% of the time in all 5 measured games against 54-90% for the opponents (473, 791, 370, 545, 608) and 83-84% for rank 1 (470; 3 scout games against rank 2, all won by 470; rank 2 60%). Tiles the team had not seen entering view per blind move: 0.64-1.03 against 1.05-1.37 (rank 1 1.12-1.49); share of the map the team has seen by r100: 51-72% against 86-93% (rank 1 92-96%). Big Empty spawns on every tile (gap 1-750), so unseen ground is where pearls wait: our dragons have a pearl in view on 22-29% of r0-99 moves there against 27-46% (rank 1 33-40%) and eat 0.067-0.095 pearls a move against 0.086-0.107 for the teams that beat us. Leader 470's dragons walk straight rays (162468 dragon 1: E for 16 rounds, then to each pearl it sees). Earlier changes to explore constants (E0086's tune, -2.7; E0068's blind-target cap, +0.9) kept the tie-break. Change, behind P.exploreKeepHeading: when choosing an explore target, prefer the candidate in the direction of the dragon's last move: add P.exploreHeadingWeight (start 1, less than one step of distance, so it breaks ties unless the coder measures that a larger value helps) times the progress a tile gives along our last heading, and optionally skip grid tiles closer than P.exploreMinDist (start 6) so a target lasts several moves (the coder measures both and says which part carries the change). A split child's heading is its birth facing. Unchanged: pearl, spawn and farm targets, the portal explore, staleness and friend terms. Boundaries: kelp ahead makes the straight tile unreachable or far by path, so the dragon turns; a teammate in view on the heading still repels through friendDist; a region smaller than P.exploreMinDist falls back to the nearest tile. Scenarios: open 64x64, a length-2 dragon that moved S with nothing seen keeps S (today W); one that moved E keeps E (today N); a wall 2 tiles ahead turns it; with a pearl in view nothing changes. Measure with a logging copy on big_empty, schooltime and 4 mix maps against the champion and swarm: explore share of turns, retargets per 10 explore turns, blind-move heading share, north share, map seen at r100 and pearls r0-99; report per-style scores (near_big_empty especially).
